caveats: **macOS and Windows `dotnet` and `jvm` legs are planned.** Only `python` ships on macOS and Windows; there `dotnet` and `jvm` read nothing and answer `status|<action>|unsupported|<os>:planned`. .NET Framework (the Windows registry family) is not covered until those legs exist, and the `dotnet` and `jvm` flavour vocabularies above are the Linux subset.

**Runtimes reachable only through an alias entry are not listed.** A framework, version or JVM home entry that is itself a symlink (Debian `default-java`, Fedora `java`) is skipped silently because its real directory is a sibling entry. A Linux `python3.<minor>` symlink is skipped too: an alternatives link leaves its real file listed as a sibling entry, while a link into another prefix is not followed, so that interpreter is not listed. A runtime reachable only through such a link is missed, while a symlink at a candidate root that is not a same-action alias is a `symlink_refused` constraint, not a skip.

**Only standard locations are walked.** `dotnet` reads `/usr/share/dotnet`, `/usr/lib/dotnet` and `/usr/lib64/dotnet`; `jvm` reads `/usr/lib/jvm`, `/opt/java`, `/usr/lib64/jvm` and `/var/opt/java`. A runtime installed elsewhere (an Oracle RPM under `/usr/java`, a version manager in a home directory, a custom prefix) is not found by design, since the plugin does not search user profiles, so `supported` with zero rows means none found at these roots. `python` reads `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `/var/usrlocal/bin` (Linux; the last is tried on every host but exists only where `/usr/local` is a symlink to `../var/usrlocal`, as on rpm-ostree hosts such as Fedora CoreOS and RHEL Edge, and is absent elsewhere), `/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions` (macOS) and `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python\PythonCore` (Windows); Homebrew, pyenv, conda, virtual environments, Xcode's `Python3.framework` and the Microsoft Store and per-user Windows installs are not walked, and other PEP 514 publishers (for example Anaconda) are not listed. A Homebrew interpreter is the `brew` ecosystem's row, and a distro or Windows Uninstall entry is the other ecosystem's row, so the same interpreter can appear in more than one source.

**Version data can be missing or partial, and is never guessed.** Some OpenJDK 8 packages ship no `release` file: Ubuntu 22.04 `openjdk-8-jre-headless`, Rocky 9 `java-1.8.0-openjdk-headless` and Alpine 3.20 `openjdk8-jre-base` were measured to ship none. Such a home is reported with version `-`, flavour `unmodelled` and `release_missing`, so the host reads `constrained` while it is installed; the `install_path` names the major, and reading the real version would need the package manager or `java -version`, which this plugin never uses. Linux `python` reports major.minor only: the row version is taken from the file name (`python3.11` reads `3.11`), and the patch level is not stored in any file the plugin can read without starting the interpreter, so it is not guessed. The Linux descriptor leg is declared `constrained` for this reason; the status row stays `supported` because the limit is known and constant, not a failed read. A symlinked `python3.X` entry (some distributions alias a minor to another) is skipped, as `python3` itself is: only regular files count. A missing or unreadable `python` version file never raises a constraint: on macOS a version directory whose `Info.plist` is absent, binary, oversized or unreadable still produces a row, with the directory's `x.y` as the version and vendor `-`, and on Windows a tag with no `Version` or `SysVersion` value reports the tag's `major.minor`; only a failure to open or list a root (or a cap) makes the result `constrained`.

**Network mounts are skipped from a dispatch-start snapshot.** A root on, under or containing a mount of a listed network type (`nfs`, `cifs`, `smb3`, `9p`, `virtiofs`, `autofs`, network `fuse.*` and others in `yuzu::shared::is_network_fstype`) is never opened, so a healthy network-mounted JDK is skipped too, and a host whose `/` is a network or virtiofs mount skips every root. The guard cannot see a mount that appears after the snapshot, a stacked filesystem such as an overlay over a dead network mount, an unlisted network type or a hang on a local block device; each can pin one of the agent's shared command workers until the kernel returns, and an unreadable mount table (`mountinfo_unreadable`) leaves the walk guarded only by the mounts read (#4875). On macOS the snapshot is `getmntinfo_r_np(MNT_NOWAIT)` (the kernel's cache, unprivileged) and a mount the system creates under `/System/Volumes/Data` is also matched by its logical spelling without that prefix; the residuals above apply there too, with one difference: a failed snapshot leaves the macOS `python` walk with no guard at all (it records `macos:runtimes:mountinfo_unreadable` and the status is `constrained`).

definitions.description: Reports installed .NET (Core/5+) shared frameworks and SDKs on Linux: one row per framework version or SDK version found under the standard install roots (flavour, version, install path), from directory names only — no `dotnet` process is started. A `supported` status with no rows means none was found at the standard roots (a runtime installed elsewhere is not looked for); a `constrained` status means a read failed or was skipped and the list may be incomplete. macOS and Windows: planned; the action answers a single unsupported status row on this OS (`status|dotnet|unsupported|<macos|windows>:planned`).

Reports installed Java runtimes on Linux: one row per JDK/JRE home under /usr/lib/jvm, /opt/java, /usr/lib64/jvm and /var/opt/java — flavour (jdk, jre, unmodelled), version, install path and vendor (the build's self-reported `IMPLEMENTOR` value, e.g. Eclipse Adoptium vs Debian; it is not verified). A home with a java binary but no `release` file (some distro OpenJDK 8 packages) is a row with version `-` and a `release_missing` constraint. No `java` process is started. A `supported` status with no rows means none was found at those roots (an Oracle-RPM /usr/java or a tarball install elsewhere is not looked for); a `constrained` status means a read failed or was skipped and the list may be incomplete. macOS and Windows: planned; the action answers a single unsupported status row on this OS (`status|jvm|unsupported|<macos|windows>:planned`).

Reports installed Python interpreters: one row per interpreter found at the standard machine roots (flavour, version, install path, vendor), from install metadata only — no `python` process is started. Windows: the python.org PEP 514 keys under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python\PythonCore in both registry views, with the full x.y.z version (per-user installs and other PEP 514 publishers are not listed). macOS: the python.org framework under /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions, with the full x.y.z from each version's Info.plist. Linux: python3.<minor> files in /usr/bin and /usr/local/bin, with major.minor ONLY (for example 3.11) — the patch level is not stored anywhere without running the interpreter, so it is not guessed. A `supported` status with no rows means none was found at those roots (Homebrew, pyenv, conda and virtual environments are not looked for); a `constrained` status means a read failed or was skipped and the list may be incomplete.

description: Installed .NET, JVM and Python runtime inventory
how_it_works:
`dotnet`, `jvm` and `python` each answer one question: which .NET, Java or Python runtimes are installed on this host. The plugin walks a fixed list of install roots and reads names and small metadata files only; it never starts `java`, `dotnet` or `python`. `dotnet` lists the `shared/<framework>/<version>` and `sdk/<version>` directory names under `/usr/share/dotnet`, `/usr/lib/dotnet` and `/usr/lib64/dotnet`. `jvm` reads the `release` file of every home under `/usr/lib/jvm`, `/opt/java`, `/usr/lib64/jvm` and `/var/opt/java`; a home that has a java binary but no `release` file (some distribution OpenJDK 8 packages) is still listed, with version `-` and a `release_missing` constraint. Every directory is opened without following symlinks, and a root on, under or containing a network mount is not opened at all. `python` ships on all three OSes: on Windows it reads the python.org PEP 514 keys under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python\PythonCore` in both registry views (per-user hives are never opened) and reports the full `x.y.z`; on macOS it lists `/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/<x.y>` and reads each version's `Resources/Info.plist` (the full `x.y.z` from `CFBundleVersion`); on Linux it lists the `python3.<minor>` regular files in `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `/var/usrlocal/bin` (all three are tried on every host; the last exists only where `/usr/local` is a symlink to `../var/usrlocal`, as on an rpm-ostree host, and is absent elsewhere) and reports **major.minor only**, because the patch level is not stored anywhere without running the interpreter (caveat 4). Each action writes one `status` row first, then zero or more runtime rows, so an empty list is never inferred from silence. On macOS and Windows `dotnet` and `jvm` answer a single `unsupported` status row. The plugin is read-only, does no vulnerability matching (a row is presence and the upstream version string, not an assessment) and does not detect runtimes embedded inside other applications such as Electron or Node bundles. The `vendor` field of `jvm` is the build's self-reported `IMPLEMENTOR` string: an input to a licensing review, not proof of the licence.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which .NET shared frameworks and SDKs are installed, and at what exact version? (`dotnet`) | One row per framework or SDK version directory under the three roots, including hosts where no package manager owns the install | Nothing: one `unsupported` row, result status `UNAVAILABLE` | Nothing, as macOS |
| Which JVMs are installed, JDK or JRE, which version, from which vendor? (`jvm`) | One row per home under the four roots; flavour and vendor come from the `release` file, so Debian and SUSE builds report flavour `unmodelled` | Nothing, as above | Nothing, as above |
| Which Python interpreters are installed, and at what version? (`python`) | One row per `python3.<minor>` file in `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `/var/usrlocal/bin` (the last exists only on rpm-ostree hosts); version is major.minor only | One row per python.org framework version, with the full `x.y.z` | One row per python.org PythonCore tag, with the full `x.y.z` |
| Is an end-of-life runtime installed on this host? | Yes, by comparing the `version` column against your own support list; the plugin attaches no verdict (a Linux Python `3.x` is enough for an end-of-life check by minor, not for a patch-level one) | Yes for `python`; not answerable for `dotnet` and `jvm` | Yes for `python`; not answerable for `dotnet` and `jvm` |

What a result proves. `supported` with zero runtime rows means none was found at the standard roots; it does not mean none is installed (a runtime in `/usr/java`, under a version manager in a home directory or in a custom prefix is not walked; for `python` that includes Homebrew, pyenv, conda, virtual environments and per-user Windows installs). `constrained` means a read failed, was skipped (a network mount) or hit a cap, so the rows may be incomplete; read the reason tokens before trusting a negative. A runtime reachable only through a symlinked alias entry can be missed (caveat 2). For the packaged-application view use `installed_apps`; for a licensing probe use `license_scan`.

### Diagrams

#### One action's walk

The mount table is read once per dispatch. A candidate on a network mount is never touched, because an open on a dead hard mount would pin one of the agent's shared command workers. The caps apply across all roots and nesting levels together, so a large tree ends the walk with `row_cap` and a `CONSTRAINED` result rather than a silent truncation. A single directory that exceeds its own entry cap also records `row_cap`, but the walk carries on with the remaining directories.

#### How a JVM home becomes a row

A home with no `release` file is only reported when a java binary proves it is a JVM, and then it carries no version: the plugin does not run `java -version`. Such a host reads `constrained` for as long as the package is installed.

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited. The first row is always `status|<action>|<level>|<reason>` (`level` is `supported`, `constrained` or `unsupported`; `reason` is comma-joined tokens, or `-`). Runtime rows follow as `<action>|<flavour>|<version>|<install_path>|<vendor>`, one per runtime found; the first field is `row_kind` (`status`, or the action name) and is the first column below. `supported` with zero runtime rows means none was found at the standard roots (caveat 3 lists what is not walked); `constrained` means a read failed or was skipped and the rows may be incomplete, so failure never reads as absent. A field the host did not supply is `-`, and every flavour mapper has a named `unmodelled` value distinct from no data. Free-text fields (`version`, `install_path`, `vendor`) go through `yuzu::util::safe_output_field`, so a value containing a pipe or ending in a backslash cannot shift the field count on the server's escape-aware decoder or on the agent's installed-software collector, which splits the python rows escape-aware too. `runtimes` is not in the server's `kKeyValuePlugins` set (`server/core/src/result_parsing.hpp`), so its rows are not decoded as two-cell key and value rows.

result_status.when: The read finished with no failure, populated, or none found at the standard roots (`status|<action>|supported|-` with zero rows): any action on Linux, `python` on macOS and Windows

One or more reads failed, were refused or skipped (a network mount), or hit a cap, and the rows returned may be incomplete; the tokens of every root are accumulated and comma-joined in the status row. `internal_error` is a caught exception on any leg: it never crosses the plugin boundary and the command returns 1 (a failed command)
macOS and Windows `dotnet` and `jvm`: the leg is not shipped; the action answers `status|<action>|unsupported|<os>:planned` and nothing else

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Every row is server instruction-result data — the standard retention policy, served over REST `/api/responses`. Nothing here is a durable server-side table of its own.

**Consumed by** the `installed_software` daily-sync source for `python` only: each `python` row becomes one `Python` entry (`kind` `app`, ecosystem `python`, `version` as reported; flavour, path and vendor are not carried). A `constrained` `python` read (a skipped network mount, an unreadable root, a cap, an access-denied registry key) withholds only the `python` rows from that day's sync; every other source's rows are still sent. The server replaces a device's stored software rows with each sync, so the stored `python` rows are removed until a read succeeds again. `dotnet` and `jvm` stay on-demand instruction results. Not consumed by TAR, DEX or metrics.

**Sensitivity.** Rows name installed runtimes with their exact version, install path and vendor, which is a patch-level and licensing-relevant software inventory for the device. The legs read only fixed machine-scope roots (`/usr`, `/opt`, `/var/opt/java`, `/var/usrlocal/bin`, `/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework`, `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python`; never a user hive or home directory) and the mount table (`/proc/self/mountinfo` on Linux, `getmntinfo_r_np` on macOS; used only to decide what to skip, never emitted), so no user-profile root is walked; `install_path` and `vendor` echo directory and file text as found, so a name planted under those roots reaches a row after the UTF-8 and pipe scrub (`yuzu::util::sanitize_utf8` replaces invalid lead and continuation bytes but still passes overlong, surrogate and out-of-range sequences that protobuf rejects: #4864).
